normalFinding.default: JVP not seen above the clavicle; column height under 3 cm above the sternal angle (estimated RAP below 8 cmH2O).

steps: Recline the patient to about 30° with the head turned slightly left.
Shine a penlight tangentially across the right side of the neck.
Find the top of the venous pulsation and measure its vertical height above the sternal angle.

normalFinding.default: Firm right upper quadrant pressure for 10 seconds: JVP rises briefly then falls back (negative hepatojugular reflux).

steps: Keep the patient reclined at 30° and breathing normally.
Press firmly over the right upper quadrant for about 10 seconds.
Watch whether the jugular column rises and stays up.

maneuvers.label: Carotid pulse palpation (one side at a time)

normalFinding.default: Carotid upstroke brisk with normal volume; symmetric bilaterally.

steps: Press gently below the angle of the jaw with your finger pads.
Assess one side, then the other — never both together.
Place the stethoscope just lateral to the midline over the carotid.
Ask the patient to hold their breath briefly while you listen.

normalFinding.default: Symmetric chest wall, no scars or deformity; no visible heaves; apical impulse not visible.

steps: Look across the chest for symmetry, scars and devices.
Look for any visible pulsation at the apex.

maneuvers.label: Precordial palpation for heaves and thrills

steps: With the patient supine, lay the flat of your fingers along the left sternal border.
Repeat at the base of the heart.
Feel for a sustained lift (heave) or a buzzing vibration (thrill).

normalFinding.default: PMI at the 5th left intercostal space, midclavicular line; small (about 2 cm), brief, not sustained.

steps: Look for the apical impulse, then feel with your finger pads.
If you cannot feel it, roll the patient onto their left side and try again.
Locate it by intercostal space and relation to the midclavicular line.

normalFinding.default: Regular rate and rhythm; normal S1 and S2; no murmurs, rubs or extra sounds.
normalFinding.cardiac_aortic: Regular rhythm; S2 crisp and well heard; no murmur.
normalFinding.cardiac_pulmonic: Regular rhythm; physiological splitting of S2 with inspiration; no murmur.
normalFinding.cardiac_mitral: Regular rhythm; S1 normal; no murmur.

steps: Press the diaphragm just firmly enough to seal against the skin.
Listen at the aortic, pulmonic, Erb point, tricuspid and mitral areas in turn.
At each area time the sounds to the cycle and listen for murmurs in systole and diastole.

normalFinding.default: No S3 or S4 with the bell.

steps: Switch to the bell and rest it lightly on the skin.
Listen over the apex (best with the patient rolled to the left) for low-pitched extra sounds.

normalFinding.foot_right: Dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses 2+.
normalFinding.foot_left: Dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses 2+.

steps: Feel each pulse with your finger pads and compare left with right.
Grade the strength (0 absent to 3+ bounding).

normalFinding.default: Warm, dry and pink; capillary refill under 2 seconds.

steps: Feel the temperature of the extremity with the back of your hand.
Press a nail bed for a few seconds, release, and time the colour return.

normalFinding.default: No edema; no pitting after firm pressure.

steps: Look at the feet, ankles and lower legs for swelling and compare sides.
Press firmly with your thumb for several seconds over a bony surface.
Check how far up any pitting extends; check the sacrum in a patient who has been lying down.
